relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: David names Ornan's threshing floor as the future temple and altar site.
Foreign residents are gathered into stone labor, exposing the vulnerable workforce beneath sacred grandeur.
Iron and bronze accumulate before construction begins.
Sidonian and Tyrian forests and workers supply cedar without number.
Solomon is young, while David prepares an enormous project meant to astonish nations.
The father summons the son into a task already defined for him.
David remembers the temple he wanted to build.
His wars and abundant bloodshed disqualify him from constructing the sacred house.
Solomon is imagined as a person of rest and peace.
Dynastic intimacy and temple work are joined in father-son covenant language.
David blesses the son toward the inherited task.
Insight and understanding matter more than architectural magnificence.
Courage is tied to Torah rather than domination.
Almost unimaginable treasure is placed before the young successor.
The project depends on many named categories of skilled labor.
Metal, craft, and command converge in the call to begin.
Political leaders are ordered to support Solomon.
David calls subjugation of the land's inhabitants rest, a claim the displaced would challenge.
The nation is directed to build a sanctuary for ark and vessels.

contemplative_note: David cannot build because violence has shaped his hands, yet the project he prepares still rests on vulnerable foreign labor, conquered land, ecological extraction, and overwhelming wealth. A truly sacred house must be judged not only by beauty but by how its workers, neighbors, forests, and young inheritors are treated.
